deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the surrounding pages: this is Riemann's heat-conduction study for the Paris prize question (the 1861 Commentatio material). The heat equation (I) is Λu = ∂u/∂t, where Λ = Σ a_{ιι'} ∂_ι∂_{ι'} + (lower order) in x1, x2, x3 and the quadratic form (a_{ιι'}) is positive definite. Assume u, written in variables α, β (and t), satisfies Δu = 0. In the present special case (β) it also satisfies a second linear equation Θu = 0. Θ contains no ∂_t and is independent of Δ.

Step 1 (end of previous page and top of this one). Take Δ = ∂_α∂_β + e∂_α + f∂_β. Then u_{αβ} = −e u_α − f u_β. Repeated use of this removes every mixed derivative from Θu. Θu then becomes a combination of pure α-derivatives and pure β-derivatives.

Step 2: two cases.
(1) All β-derivatives drop out (or, symmetrically, all α-derivatives). This gives an ODE in α with coefficients depending on α, β: Σ_ν a_ν(α,β) ∂^ν u/∂α^ν = 0.
(2) Otherwise, one obtains an ODE in t: Σ_ν a_ν(α,β) ∂^ν u/∂t^ν = 0.
Riemann's argument for (2): ∂_t^k u = Λ^k u. Using Δu = 0 and Θu = 0, each Λ^k u can be rewritten using only pure α- and pure β-derivatives of order not exceeding those in Θ. That set is finite. So finitely many of u, ∂_t u, ∂_t^2 u, … are linearly dependent over functions of (α, β). Eliminating gives (2).
My filling of the implicit step: in case (2) both a top α-term A_p ∂_α^p and a top β-term B_q ∂_β^q are present in reduced Θ. Differentiating Θu = 0 and re-reducing mixed terms via Δ expresses ∂_α^{p+1}u, ∂_β^{q+1}u, etc. through lower ones. Hence the span is finite-dimensional.

Step 3: special forms of Δ.
- Δ = ∂_α^2 + e∂_α + f∂_β with f ≠ 0. Use u_β = −(u_{αα} + e u_α)/f to remove all β-derivatives from both Θu and Λu. Either form can then be reached.
- f = 0. Δu = 0 is itself an ODE in α, so this belongs to case (1). The same holds for Δ = ∂_α.

Step 4: case (2) examined. The general solution of a linear ODE in t whose coefficients do not depend on t is a finite sum of terms f(t) e^{λt}. Here f is a polynomial in t and λ is independent of t (it may depend on x).
Terms with different λ are independent. Hence each group satisfies (I) separately; Riemann calls this easy to see.
Claim: λ cannot be a non-constant function of x1, x2, x3. Let k t^n be the leading term of f.
Case 1°: λ is real, or λ = μ + iν with μ, ν functions of a single real function α(x). Substitute u = f(t) e^{λt} into the left side of (I). The second-order part of Λ yields t^2 ∂_ιλ ∂_{ι'}λ. So the highest power present is t^{n+2} e^{λt}, with coefficient k λ'(α)^2 Σ a_{ιι'} ∂_ια ∂_{ι'}α. This is completed on the next page.
The right side ∂_t u reaches only t^n e^{λt}. So this coefficient must vanish. Positive definiteness then forces ∇α = 0 (or λ' = 0), i.e. λ is constant.
Case 2° (μ, ν independent) follows on the next page.
errors: No real errors. The page asserts two things without proof: that the reduced derivatives form a finite set, and that each exponential group separately satisfies (I). Both are true; the first needs the top α- and β-terms of the reduced Θ to be nonzero, which is exactly what the 'sin minus' case guarantees.

In 1°, for complex λ = μ + iν, the vanishing of λ'(α)^2 Q(∇α) gives either λ' = 0 or Q(∇α) = 0. Positive definiteness of the real form handles the second option. Riemann compresses this by writing the coefficient as k(∂λ/∂α)^2 Q(∇α).

results.what: Reduction of a second linear constraint Θu = 0 modulo Δu = 0 to pure derivatives; dichotomy between an ODE in a spatial variable and an ODE in t, via finite dimensionality of the space spanned by Λ^k u
results.modern_name: Compatibility / finite-dimensional differential module argument (elimination in the theory of overdetermined linear PDE systems)
results.usually_credited_to: General elimination ideas: Riemann (here), later Riquier, Janet, Cartan

results.what: Solutions of a linear ODE in t with t-independent coefficients are sums of polynomial times exponential terms
results.modern_name: Quasi-polynomial (exponential-polynomial) solutions of constant-coefficient linear ODEs

results.what: The exponent λ in a solution f(t)e^{λ(x)t} of a heat equation with positive definite principal part must be constant: the leading t^{n+2} coefficient k Q(∇λ) must vanish
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, Paris prize essay 1861 (published in the Werke, 1876)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the classification in Riemann's 1861 Paris prize essay on heat conduction (when isothermal surfaces remain isothermal), which was published in his Werke. The finiteness/elimination argument and the leading-coefficient argument are clever but belong to known Riemann material.
